sections.text: Google successfully booted up its Project Suncatcher prototype satellite, which launched into orbit aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. sections.text: The project explores whether data centres can operate in space to process distributed AI workloads. Google aims to test whether inference workloads remain viable under these real-world conditions rather than ground simulations.

He faces an identity crisis and family reunions as his epic mission ends.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Karl Bushby set off from Punta Arenas in Chile in 1998 to walk an unbroken path to Hull. Over 28 years and 36,000 miles, he crossed four continents, traversed the Darién Gap and Bering Strait, and recently swam the English Channel to land in Dover.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The journey tested physical and mental endurance through jungles, freezing straits, and geopolitical delays. Bushby now faces a major identity crisis as he transitions away from the mission that defined half his life.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Bushby is completing his final few miles in Lincolnshire and will be reunited with his family in Hull, including his son, granddaughter, and mother.

articles.title: He questioned Thailand's monarchy dressed as Harry Potter. Now he's in jail for 34 years
articles.standfirst: Thailand has prosecuted 294 people since 2020 under its lèse majesté law, with sentences going up to 50 years.

gist: Human rights lawyer Arnon Nampa received a cumulative sentence of over 34 years in prison.
His offence was violating Thailand's strict lèse majesté law by questioning the monarchy in 2020.
The law has been used extensively against student protesters, leading many to flee into exile.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Arnon Nampa, a human rights lawyer, was sentenced to a further prison term under Thailand's lèse majesté law, bringing his total sentence to more than 34 years. He was prosecuted for a 2020 speech where he dressed as Harry Potter and called for public scrutiny of the monarchy.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The law has been used in hundreds of prosecutions since 2020 to smother public discussion about the monarchy. Courts interpret the law broadly, and defendants face severe sentences and difficulties mounting a defence.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Dozens of activists remain on trial or have fled into exile to avoid imprisonment. Arnon faces pending verdicts in additional cases and may spend his entire life in prison.
